bull.b: Strong TTM revenue growth alongside higher gross margins indicates improving customer adoption and a more scalable offering. If maintained, this combination can expand contribution from each deployment, support reinvestment, and create a stronger foundation for eventual operating leverage.

Recurring revenue is becoming a larger and faster-growing part of the business, improving visibility relative to project-based deployments. A greater mix of contracted, repeatable revenue can strengthen retention, support higher margins, and make future cash generation more predictable.

Material reductions across G&A, sales and marketing, and R&D have sharply narrowed the adjusted EBITDA loss. Continued savings, combined with recurring revenue growth, could provide meaningful operating leverage and improve the company’s ability to reach management’s targeted profitability.

bear.b: The company remains materially unprofitable even after improving its revenue and margin trends. Sustained operating and net losses reduce financial resilience, limit internally funded investment, and leave the long-term business case dependent on successful execution toward break-even.

bear.t: Negative cash generation and funding dependence
bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued cash consumption can constrain product investment and increase reliance on cost reductions or external financing, while refinancing uncertainty adds risk to maintaining adequate liquidity.

Regulatory scrutiny over data retention, sharing, access, and litigation risk creates a structural go-to-market hurdle for ALPR solutions. Longer sales cycles and uncertain government procurement can delay bookings, complicate forecasting, and slow conversion of the active pipeline.
